---
title: "MORA Paradise - 3D Catchment Views"
author: "ROSSyndicate"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

This R markdown builds 3D views of the three candidate source catchments for the
Paradise water system (Edith Current, Edith Downstream, and Paradise GW) from the
Washington Geological Survey lidar DTM, with vertical exaggeration and either
draped aerial imagery or a shaded-relief texture. A second view sets the
catchments against Mount Rainier using a coarser public DEM.

Rendering uses {rayshader}. On macOS, {rgl} and {rayrender} need XQuartz
(<https://www.xquartz.org>) to load, even when no window is opened. Install it
once (`brew install --cask xquartz`, then log out and back in).

# 1. Setup

```{r setup}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE,
                      message = FALSE,
                      warning = FALSE,
                      eval = TRUE)

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())

source(here::here("Reports/report_setup.R"))

# Render off-screen by default. Set TRUE for a live window you can rotate by
# hand; this needs XQuartz running (log out and back in after installing it),
# otherwise rgl crashes the R session when it opens the window. Restart R after
# changing it, since rgl reads this option when it loads.
open_window <- FALSE
options(rgl.useNULL = !open_window)
library(rayshader)

```

## - Figure settings

Everything that controls the look of the figures is set here.

```{r settings}

# Vertical exaggeration (1 = true relief). 2 reads well for this relief.
z_exag <- 2

# Lidar is 1.5 ft; aggregate by this factor for rendering (6 -> 9 ft cells).
# Lower for more detail, at the cost of memory and render time.
dem_agg <- 6

# Buffer around the Paradise River catchment for the basin view (ft)
aoi_buffer_ft <- 1500

# Surface texture: "imagery" (Esri World Imagery) or "hillshade"
drape <- "imagery"

# Catchment styling: outline width (texture pixels) and fill opacity. The
# catchments are nested, so the fill deepens toward Edith Current.
outline_width <- 8
fill_alpha <- 0.18

# Imagery tile zoom (16 is ~2 m per pixel at this latitude)
imagery_zoom <- 16

# Camera for the basin view: theta = compass direction the camera sits on,
# measured as rotation around the scene (0 = looking north from the south),
# phi = elevation angle above the horizon, zoom < 1 moves in.
cam_basin <- list(theta = -43, phi = 28, zoom = 0.74, fov = 40)
cam_mountain <- list(theta = 15, phi = 25, zoom = 0.65, fov = 40)

# Preview mode: TRUE shows a quick software render (a few seconds) in the plot
# pane instead of the path-traced figure, for tuning the camera. Set FALSE for
# the final figures.
preview <- TRUE

# Output size (px) and path tracer samples for render_highquality()
out_width <- 2200
out_height <- 1800
hq_samples <- 256

# Catchment colors match the other report figures
system_colors <- c("Edith Current"    = "#1b6ca8",
                   "Edith Downstream" = "#459a74",
                   "Paradise GW"      = "#a1631f")

# Callout boxes for the basin view. Boxes sit in the white space above the
# terrain; box_x and box_y are the box centers as fractions of the image width
# and height (from the top left). Each leader line runs to a point on that
# catchment's own outline, skipping stretches drawn over by a smaller nested
# catchment: the point nearest aim_x/aim_y if given, otherwise nearest the box.
# Adjust these after changing the camera.
callouts <- tibble::tribble(
  ~system,            ~label,              ~box_x, ~box_y, ~aim_x, ~aim_y,
  "Edith Downstream", "Edith Downstream",   0.10,   0.24,   NA,     NA,
  "Edith Current",    "Current Catchment",  0.45,   0.15,   NA,     NA,
  "Paradise GW",      "Paradise Valley",    0.70,   0.25,   NA,     NA
)

# White band added above the render to hold the callouts (fraction of the
# render height). Set to 0 if the camera already leaves enough sky.
callout_band <- 0.10

fig_dir <- "data/park/MORA/Figs"

```

# 2. Catchments, streams, and outlets

Same catchment files as `MORA_Deep_Dive_workflow.Rmd`. The lidar DTM is in
Washington State Plane South (US ft), which is close to north-up here, so the
vectors are projected to the DEM rather than the other way around.

```{r vectors}

dem_path <- "data/park/MORA/lidar_DTM_paradise.tif"
dem_crs <- terra::crs(terra::rast(dem_path))

catchments <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sf::st_read("data/park/MORA/edithcreek_watershed.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(system = "Edith Current"),
  sf::st_read("data/park/MORA/downstream_edithcreek/downstream_edithcreek_watershed.gpkg",
              quiet = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(system = "Edith Downstream"),
  sf::st_read("data/park/MORA/paradise_river/paradise_river_watershed.gpkg",
              quiet = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(system = "Paradise GW")
) %>%
  dplyr::select(system) %>%
  sf::st_transform(dem_crs) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(system = factor(system, levels = names(system_colors)))

streams <- sf::st_read("data/park/MORA/paradise_river_streams.gpkg", quiet = TRUE) %>%
  sf::st_transform(dem_crs)

# Outlets: the existing Edith Creek intake (water system database) and the
# snapped pour points used to delineate the two downstream catchments
current_intake <- get_wsd() %>%
  dplyr::filter(park_unit == "MORA",
                grepl("Paradise", water_system_name)) %>%
  sf::st_transform(dem_crs) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(system = "Edith Current")

outlets <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  current_intake,
  sf::st_read("data/park/MORA/downstream_edithcreek/downstream_edithcreek_snapped_pour_point.shp",
              quiet = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(system = "Edith Downstream") %>%
    sf::st_transform(dem_crs),
  sf::st_read("data/park/MORA/paradise_river/paradise_river_snapped_pour_point.shp",
              quiet = TRUE) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(system = "Paradise GW") %>%
    sf::st_transform(dem_crs)
) %>%
  sf::st_zm() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(system = factor(system, levels = names(system_colors)))

```

# 3. Helper functions

`drape_texture()` builds the surface texture for a DEM, and `add_catchments()`
adds the catchment outlines, streams, and outlets on top. Outlines get a white
halo so they read on both imagery and shaded relief.

```{r helpers}

# Esri World Imagery tiles warped onto the DEM grid, as an RGB array in [0, 1]
get_imagery <- function(dem, zoom) {
  aoi <- sf::st_as_sfc(sf::st_bbox(dem)) %>%
    sf::st_transform(4326)
  tiles <- maptiles::get_tiles(aoi, provider = "Esri.WorldImagery",
                               zoom = zoom, crop = TRUE)
  img <- terra::project(tiles[[1:3]], dem, method = "bilinear")
  arr <- terra::as.array(img) / 255
  arr[is.na(arr)] <- 0
  pmin(pmax(arr, 0), 1)
}

drape_texture <- function(dem, elmat, drape, zscale, zoom = 16) {
  # Terrain shadows are computed at true relief so the sun angle looks natural
  shadow <- ray_shade(elmat, zscale = zscale, sunaltitude = 35,
                      sunangle = 225, multicore = TRUE)
  ambient <- ambient_shade(elmat, zscale = zscale, multicore = TRUE)
  if (drape == "imagery") {
    get_imagery(dem, zoom) %>%
      add_shadow(shadow, max_darken = 0.4) %>%
      add_shadow(ambient, max_darken = 0.2)
  } else {
    # Muted hypsometric tint from valley forest to alpine rock and snow
    hypso <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(
      c("#4f6b4a", "#7d8f62", "#b3ad86", "#d8d0bc", "#f4f2ee"))(256)
    elmat %>%
      height_shade(texture = hypso) %>%
      add_shadow(lamb_shade(elmat, zscale = zscale, sunangle = 225), 0.3) %>%
      add_shadow(shadow, max_darken = 0.5) %>%
      add_shadow(ambient, max_darken = 0.2)
  }
}

add_catchments <- function(texture, elmat, extent, line_scale = 2) {
  out <- texture
  # Streams first so the catchment outlines sit on top
  out <- add_overlay(out, generate_line_overlay(
    streams, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
    color = "#9fd3ff", 
    linewidth = 2.5 * line_scale))
  # Largest catchment first; the nested ones draw over it
  for (s in rev(levels(catchments$system))) {
    poly <- dplyr::filter(catchments, system == s)
    edge <- sf::st_cast(poly, "MULTILINESTRING")
    out <- out %>%
      add_overlay(generate_polygon_overlay(poly, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
                                           palette = system_colors[[s]],
                                           linecolor = NA),
                  alphalayer = fill_alpha) %>%
      add_overlay(generate_line_overlay(edge, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
                                        color = "white",
                                        linewidth = (outline_width + 5) * line_scale)) %>%
      add_overlay(generate_line_overlay(edge, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
                                        color = system_colors[[s]],
                                        linewidth = outline_width * line_scale))
  }
  for (s in levels(outlets$system)) {
    pt <- dplyr::filter(outlets, system == s)
    out <- out %>%
      add_overlay(generate_point_overlay(pt, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
                                         color = "white", size = 7 * line_scale)) %>%
      add_overlay(generate_point_overlay(pt, extent = extent, heightmap = elmat,
                                         color = system_colors[[s]],
                                         size = 4.5 * line_scale))
  }
  out
}

# Candidate leader-line targets: points along each catchment outline, dropping
# stretches within `shared_ft` of a smaller catchment's outline. The nested
# catchments share parts of their ridges, and the smaller one is drawn on top,
# so those stretches show in the smaller catchment's color.
outline_points <- function(spacing_ft = 30, shared_ft = 60) {
  edge <- function(s) {
    catchments %>%
      dplyr::filter(system %in% s) %>%
      sf::st_geometry() %>%
      sf::st_boundary() %>%
      sf::st_union()
  }
  lv <- levels(catchments$system)   # smallest first
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(lv), function(i) {
    s <- lv[i]
    pts <- edge(s) %>%
      sf::st_cast("MULTILINESTRING") %>%
      sf::st_cast("LINESTRING") %>%
      sf::st_line_sample(density = 1 / spacing_ft)
    pts <- sf::st_cast(pts[!sf::st_is_empty(pts)], "POINT")
    keep <- rep(TRUE, length(pts))
    if (i > 1) {
      keep <- as.numeric(sf::st_distance(pts, edge(lv[seq_len(i - 1)]))) > shared_ft
    }
    sf::st_sf(system = s, geometry = pts[keep])
  })
}

# Position of map points in the rendered image (fractions of width and height
# from the top left). Uses rayshader's scene coordinates (x = DEM column and
# z = DEM row, both centered; y = elevation / zscale) and the current rgl
# camera, which render_highquality() and render_snapshot() also use.
project_to_image <- function(pts, dem, zscale) {
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(pts)[, 1:2, drop = FALSE]
  cell <- terra::res(dem)[1]
  elev <- terra::extract(dem, xy)[, 1]
  scene <- cbind((xy[, 1] - terra::xmin(dem)) / cell - terra::ncol(dem) / 2,
                 elev / zscale,
                 (terra::ymax(dem) - xy[, 2]) / cell - terra::nrow(dem) / 2)
  m <- rgl::par3d(c("modelMatrix", "projMatrix"))
  h <- cbind(scene, 1) %*% t(m$projMatrix %*% m$modelMatrix)
  data.frame(fx = (h[, 1] / h[, 4] + 1) / 2,
             fy = 1 - (h[, 2] / h[, 4] + 1) / 2)
}

# Callout boxes with leader lines drawn onto a rendered image. `targets` are
# outline points with their image positions (fx, fy); each box connects to the
# target of its catchment closest to the box.
add_callouts <- function(png_in, png_out, targets, band = callout_band) {
  img <- magick::image_read(png_in)
  info <- magick::image_info(img)
  w <- info$width
  pad <- round(band * info$height)
  if (pad > 0) {
    img <- magick::image_append(c(magick::image_blank(w, pad, "white"), img),
                                stack = TRUE)
  }
  h <- info$height + pad
  s <- w / 2400
  img <- magick::image_draw(img)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(callouts))) {
    col <- system_colors[[callouts$system[i]]]
    bx <- callouts$box_x[i] * w
    by <- callouts$box_y[i] * h
    tg <- dplyr::filter(targets, system == callouts$system[i])
    tx <- tg$fx * w
    ty <- tg$fy * info$height + pad
    aim_x <- dplyr::coalesce(callouts$aim_x[i], callouts$box_x[i]) * w
    aim_y <- dplyr::coalesce(callouts$aim_y[i], callouts$box_y[i]) * h
    j <- which.min((tx - aim_x)^2 + (ty - aim_y)^2)
    cex <- 3 * s
    # image_draw() flips the y axis, so text heights come back negative
    half_w <- abs(strwidth(callouts$label[i], cex = cex, font = 2)) / 2 + 28 * s
    half_h <- abs(strheight(callouts$label[i], cex = cex, font = 2)) / 2 + 20 * s
    # Leader starts at the point on the box edge closest to its target
    sx <- min(max(tx[j], bx - half_w), bx + half_w)
    sy <- min(max(ty[j], by - half_h), by + half_h)
    segments(sx, sy, tx[j], ty[j], col = "white", lwd = 7 * s)
    segments(sx, sy, tx[j], ty[j], col = col, lwd = 3.5 * s)
    points(tx[j], ty[j], pch = 21, bg = col, col = "white", cex = 2.2 * s, lwd = 3 * s)
    rect(bx - half_w, by - half_h, bx + half_w, by + half_h,
         col = "white", border = col, lwd = 4 * s)
    text(bx, by, callouts$label[i], cex = cex, font = 2, col = "gray15")
  }
  dev.off()
  magick::image_write(img, png_out)
  png_out
}

# Legend strip, exaggeration note, and data credits added below the render
add_legend <- function(png_in, png_out, credit) {
  img <- magick::image_read(png_in)
  w <- magick::image_info(img)$width
  s <- w / 2400
  bar_h <- round(150 * s)
  bar <- magick::image_blank(w, bar_h, "white")
  x <- round(60 * s)
  for (nm in names(system_colors)) {
    bar <- bar %>%
      magick::image_draw()
    rect(x, bar_h * 0.30, x + 70 * s, bar_h * 0.30 + 16 * s,
         col = system_colors[[nm]], border = NA)
    text(x + 85 * s, bar_h * 0.30 + 8 * s, nm, adj = c(0, 0.5),
         cex = 2.6 * s, font = 2, col = "gray15")
    dev.off()
    x <- x + 650 * s
  }
  bar <- bar %>%
    magick::image_annotate(
      paste0("Vertical exaggeration ", z_exag, "x."),
      size = round(30 * s), color = "gray25",
      location = paste0("+", round(60 * s), "+", round(80 * s))) %>%
    magick::image_annotate(credit, size = round(26 * s), color = "gray40",
                           location = paste0("+", round(60 * s), "+", round(115 * s)))
  magick::image_append(c(img, bar), stack = TRUE) %>%
    magick::image_write(png_out)
  png_out
}

```

# 4. Basin view from the lidar DTM

Crop the lidar to the Paradise River catchment plus a buffer, convert elevations
to the horizontal unit (both are US ft, so no conversion is needed), and
aggregate for rendering.

```{r basin_dem}

aoi <- catchments %>%
  sf::st_union() %>%
  sf::st_buffer(aoi_buffer_ft) %>%
  sf::st_bbox()

dem_basin <- terra::rast(dem_path) %>%
  terra::crop(terra::ext(aoi[["xmin"]], aoi[["xmax"]], aoi[["ymin"]], aoi[["ymax"]])) %>%
  terra::aggregate(fact = dem_agg, fun = "mean", na.rm = TRUE)

# Cell size and elevation are both in US ft
cell_ft <- terra::res(dem_basin)[1]
zscale_true <- cell_ft
zscale_plot <- cell_ft / z_exag

elmat_basin <- raster_to_matrix(dem_basin)
dim(elmat_basin)
range(elmat_basin, na.rm = TRUE)

```

```{r basin_texture}

tex_basin <- drape_texture(dem_basin, elmat_basin, drape = drape,
                           zscale = zscale_true, zoom = imagery_zoom) %>%
  add_catchments(elmat_basin, extent = terra::ext(dem_basin))

# Flat map of the same texture, useful for checking overlays
#plot_map(tex_basin)

```

```{r basin_render}

rgl::close3d()
plot_3d(tex_basin, elmat_basin,
        zscale = zscale_plot,
        solid = TRUE, soliddepth = "auto", solidcolor = "gray35",
        solidlinecolor = "gray25",
        shadow = TRUE, shadowdepth = "auto", shadowcolor = "gray75",
        background = "white",
        # Same aspect as the output, so the callout positions line up
        windowsize = c(out_width, out_height) / 2)

render_camera(theta = cam_basin$theta, phi = cam_basin$phi,
              zoom = cam_basin$zoom, fov = cam_basin$fov)

basin_targets <- outline_points()
basin_targets <- dplyr::bind_cols(sf::st_drop_geometry(basin_targets),
                                  project_to_image(basin_targets, dem_basin, zscale_plot))

basin_raw <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0("catchment_3d_basin_", drape, "_raw.png"))

basin_callout_png <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0("catchment_3d_basin_", drape, "_callouts.png"))
if (preview) {
  preview_png <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  render_snapshot(filename = preview_png, software_render = TRUE,
                  width = out_width / 2, height = out_height / 2)
  add_callouts(preview_png, preview_png, basin_targets)
  plot(magick::image_read(preview_png))
} else {
  render_highquality(filename = basin_raw,
                     samples = hq_samples,
                     width = out_width, height = out_height,
                     lightdirection = c(225, 45), lightaltitude = c(55,60),
                     lightintensity = c(700, 250), lightcolor = c("white", "white"),
                     interactive = FALSE, preview = FALSE)

  add_callouts(basin_raw, basin_callout_png, basin_targets)
  add_legend(basin_callout_png,
             file.path(fig_dir, paste0("catchment_3d_basin_", drape, ".png")),
             credit = paste0("Elevation: Washington Geological Survey lidar DTM. ",
                             if (drape == "imagery") "Imagery: Esri World Imagery."
                             else "Shaded relief from the lidar DTM."))
}

```

# 5. Mountain context view

The lidar stops below the upper mountain, so this view uses the AWS Terrain
Tiles (USGS 3DEP in the U.S.) through {elevatr} at roughly 10 m to place the
catchments below the summit. The extent runs from below the Paradise River
outlet to just north of the summit.

```{r mountain_dem}

mtn_aoi <- sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = -121.84, ymin = 46.755,
                         xmax = -121.65, ymax = 46.875),
                       crs = sf::st_crs(4326)) %>%
  sf::st_as_sfc() %>%
  sf::st_as_sf()

dem_mtn <- elevatr::get_elev_raster(mtn_aoi, z = 14, src = "aws", clip = "bbox") %>%
  terra::rast() %>%
  terra::project(dem_crs, res = 33) # ~10 m cells in US ft

# elevatr returns meters; convert to US ft to match the horizontal unit
dem_mtn <- dem_mtn / 0.3048006
dem_mtn <- terra::trim(dem_mtn)

elmat_mtn <- raster_to_matrix(dem_mtn)
cell_mtn <- terra::res(dem_mtn)[1]
dim(elmat_mtn)

```

```{r mountain_render}

tex_mtn <- drape_texture(dem_mtn, elmat_mtn, drape = drape,
                         zscale = cell_mtn, zoom = imagery_zoom - 2) %>%
  add_catchments(elmat_mtn, extent = terra::ext(dem_mtn), line_scale = 1.3)

plot_map(tex_mtn)

rgl::close3d()
plot_3d(tex_mtn, elmat_mtn,
        zscale = cell_mtn / z_exag,
        solid = TRUE, soliddepth = "auto", solidcolor = "gray35",
        solidlinecolor = "gray25",
        shadow = TRUE, shadowdepth = "auto", shadowcolor = "gray75",
        background = "white",
        windowsize = c(1400, 950))
render_camera(theta = cam_mountain$theta, phi = cam_mountain$phi,
              zoom = cam_mountain$zoom, fov = cam_mountain$fov)

mtn_raw <- file.path(fig_dir, paste0("catchment_3d_mountain_", drape, "_raw.png"))
if (preview) {
  render_snapshot(software_render = TRUE,
                  width = out_width / 2, height = out_height / 2)
} else {
  render_highquality(filename = mtn_raw,
                     samples = hq_samples,
                     width = out_width, height = out_height,
                     lightdirection = 225, lightaltitude = 40,
                     lightintensity = 650, lightcolor = "white",
                     interactive = FALSE, preview = FALSE)

  add_legend(mtn_raw,
             file.path(fig_dir, paste0("catchment_3d_mountain_", drape, ".png")),
             credit = paste0("Elevation: USGS 3DEP via AWS Terrain Tiles. ",
                             if (drape == "imagery") "Imagery: Esri World Imagery."
                             else "Shaded relief from the DEM."))
}

```

# 6. Orbit animation (optional)

An orbit around the basin view for presentations. `render_movie()` captures the
rgl window, so it needs an interactive session with XQuartz.

```{r basin_movie, eval = FALSE}

plot_3d(tex_basin, elmat_basin, zscale = zscale_plot,
        solid = TRUE, shadow = TRUE, background = "white",
        windowsize = c(1400, 950))
render_movie(filename = file.path(fig_dir, "catchment_3d_basin_orbit.mp4"),
             type = "orbit", frames = 360, fps = 30,
             phi = cam_basin$phi, zoom = cam_basin$zoom, fov = cam_basin$fov)

```
